text:
sarah: Heads-up — Acme (customer) reports intermittent 403s on embeddings endpoint since they migrated some workloads from project `proj-old` -> `proj-new`. They claim they didn’t rotate keys, just switched the org/project header in their proxy. Seen in our agent logs as an auth error: "org_mismatch". Sample req ids: req_1705001200-ab12, req_1705001321-cd34, req_1705001405-ef56. Can we get repro guidance and what exact logs/debug bundle we need?

lee: Can you paste the raw request headers from one of the failed requests (including Authorization and any X- headers)? Also give the time window (UTC) for those req ids. Most likely causes: service key scoped to proj-old but header says proj-new, or ingress proxy is rewriting/stripping the X-Redwood-Org header.

sarah: Time window: 2024-11-11T18:00:00Z — 2024-11-11T18:10:00Z. Here's the curl customer used (they said it fails ~30% of the time):

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABCDEF" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-acme-new" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"embed-large","input":"hello"}'
```

They also tried omitting X-Redwood-Org and got a 401. When it fails we see this line in agent logs: `auth_error=org_mismatch svc_key=svc-acme token_org=org-acme-old header_org=org-acme-new request_id=req_1705001321-cd34`.

julian: Two quick repros to narrow root cause: (1) Verify token->org mapping: run the token inspect endpoint from their network and confirm it returns `org-acme-old`. (2) Reproduce curl but force the header to match the token's org. e.g.

```bash
# simulate token still scoped to old org
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABCDEF" -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-acme-old" \n  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-large","input":"test"}'
```

If that consistently succeeds then it's header mismatch. If it still fails intermittently, suspect intermediate proxy/load-balancer is occasionally dropping or canonicalizing the header. Ask them to run curl -v and capture the full request/response including `> Authorization` and `> X-Redwood-Org` lines.

lee: Also ask network team to check the ingress rewrite rollout (we rolled a fix two days ago that canonicalizes some headers for security). infra-bot, can you paste the rollout id and whether X-Redwood-Org was on the allowlist?

infra-bot: Rollout r-2024-11-09-682 applied to ingress: header_canonicalization=true, allowlist=[Host,Content-Type,Authorization,User-Agent]. X-Redwood-Org was NOT in the allowlist by default. Change r-2024-11-10-191 added a temporary passthrough for X-Redwood-Org in region-us-east-1 (deploy id: dpl-8812). See internal link: https://ci.redwood/infradeploys/r-2024-11-09-682 (internal).

lee: That matches hypothesis — some edge nodes still running old config might strip X-Redwood-Org. Two immediate asks for customer repro bundle:
- exact failing request ids (you already provided three — good)
- full agent logs for 5 minutes before/after each req id (agent.log lines including auth debug level)
- TLS/ELB request ids (ELB-RequestId header) if available
- client curl -v output showing the outbound headers from their client
- their NAT/egress IPs so we can correlate with ingress nodes

support-bot: Please attach a debug bundle named `acme-orgmix-1705001234` containing: time_range=2024-11-11T17:55:00Z/2024-11-11T18:15:00Z, request_ids=[req_1705001200-ab12,req_1705001321-cd34,req_1705001405-ef56], customer_org=org-acme-new, token_sample=sk_live_ABCDEF (redact full secret in bundle). Include: agent.log, ingress logs for region-us-east-1, ELB logs, and client-provided curl -v output.

julian: For reproduction steps we should ask the customer to run a quick targeted test that toggles header variants and logs responses: 20 requests with header matching token org, 20 with header set to new org, and 20 without X-Redwood-Org. Preferably from same machine so egress IP constant. Save the responses and note which requests returned 200 vs 401/403. Include time stamps and exact curl commands. Example script we asked them to run: 

```bash
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total} %{url_effective}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABCDEF" -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-acme-old" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings &
done
wait
```

sarah: I'll get the customer to run the script and attach the curl -v output + their NAT IPs. Also will request they run the token-inspect endpoint and paste the JSON (will redact secret).

lee: Once we have bundle + curl outputs we'll correlate request ids to ingress node IDs and see which nodes still have the older ingress config. If confirmed, we can either (a) whitelist X-Redwood-Org across all nodes, or (b) do token-org reconciliation fallback for svc keys during a short mitigation window.

sarah: Thanks — pinging @acct-team to get permission to pull ELB logs for their account and asking customer to run the tests. Will upload debug bundle here when I have it. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Debug checklist: include region, customer org id, request ids, curl -v stdout, agent.log excerpt, ingress node ids. Bundle request id: dbg-1705001234-acme.

sarah: Uploading bundle now (dbg-1705001234-acme). Attaching the customer's curl-v output (redacted) and NAT IPs. I'll follow up when infra confirms which nodes still have old config.

julian: Great — once infra confirms we should schedule a small config push and monitor for error rate drop. If anyone needs me to validate the token->org mapping logic in auth service, I can help.

lee: Thanks team. Follow-up: if we see a large cohort of affected requests, we may need an automatic fallback that validates org via service key metadata for a short period to avoid customer downtime. We'll triage after bundle analysis.

infra-bot: Note: changed allowlist rollout is staged, ETA full roll-out ~2024-11-12T02:00:00Z.

sarah: Closing loop for now — collecting bundle + customer test results. Will reopen if we see more failures after infra roll-out.
